To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a retinal image registration method can be built that is initialized by just a few landmark correspondences and is capable of registering retinal images with subpixel accuracy.

(i) a new, automatic retinal image alignment algorithm is presented that bootstraps the estimation of the parameters of an inter-image transformation model from just one or two retinal image landmark pairs; and (ii) this new algorithm achieves sub-pixel registration accuracy in just a few minutes.

a) the use of a high-order transformation model is necessary for accurate registration of retinal images, and b) a high-order transformation can be estimated from a small number of landmark correspondences by bootstrapping the transformation parameters from low-order transformations.
In summary, our research is concerned with
developing algorithms to register retinal images.
the development of a new retinal feature extraction and image registration algorithm that can be applied to images of diseased retinas.
the development of an automatic, robust, fast, and accurate retinal image registration method for use with feature-poor, diseased eyes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a new retinal registration method was developed that uses just one or two retinal landmark correspondences to initialize a covariance-driven, high-order registration.
the proposed registration algorithm is a fast and robust algorithm for retinal image registration that can be initialized from small sets, even just one or two, landmark correspondences.
the proposed method is a novel, fast and accurate retinal image registration method that is able to cope with the challenges posed by feature-poor retinal images.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the new registration algorithm can register images with high accuracy and speed using just one or two landmark correspondences.
we have developed a retinal image registration method based on the covariance matrix of a high-order transformation model, which is bootstrapped from just one or two landmark correspondences.
we have developed an algorithm that registers images of diseased retinas using just one or two landmark correspondences, and which is fast and accurate enough to be used in a clinical setting.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a covariance-based model selection approach can bootstrap a high-quality transformation model from just a small set of landmark correspondences.

, by exploiting the covariance matrix of estimated parameters, we can bootstrap a high-order model from very little information, and that this is especially useful for the registration of retinal images.
, in the context of retinal image registration, a covariance-based model selection approach can be successfully applied to a high-order, non-linear transformation.
